1	# Phase-2 batch-3 judge brief — LLM-as-judge scoring pass (H268 WS-C1)
2	
3	_Created: 07-07-2026 · Last updated: 07-07-2026_
4	
5	You are a judge agent (Sonnet 5) scoring ALREADY-DRAFTED commentator-note candidates. You did NOT
6	draft them (drafter ≠ judge). Your default stance is **refute**: a note must EARN `keep`. Canonical
7	rubric: [docs/PHASE2_METHOD.md §3.4](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/PHASE2_METHOD.md);
8	method provenance: [docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md).
9	
10	## Inputs (per sarga NN, worktree-relative)
11	
12	1. `data/analysis/phase2_batch3/sarga_NN_candidates.json` — the notes to judge (and the drafter's
13	   rejects — do not re-judge rejects).
14	2. `data/analysis/phase2_batch3/segmented/sarga_NN_segmented.json` — the verse bundles: the cited
15	   commentator's Devanagari text (ground truth for faithfulness), `sanskrit_iast`, `leonov_ru`,
16	   `pratika_check` (anchoring state).
17	3. `data/leonov_own_notes.json` (slice `"sarga" == NN`) + `data/sundara_commentary_to_add.json`
18	   (slice `"shloka"` starts `"V.NN."`) — the non-triviality baseline (tier-1 + Phase-1).
19	
20	## Procedure per note (reason FIRST, then score)
21	
22	For each note in `notes[]`: read the bundle for its `verse_id`; locate the cited commentator's
23	text; then write a 1–2-clause reason and score each axis 0–2:
24	
25	- `faithfulness` — is EVERY claim in the note entailed by the cited commentary text? Misattributed
26	  commentator, invented gloss, or overstated claim ⇒ 0. Minor wording overreach ⇒ 1. **Gate: must
27	  be 2, else verdict `reject`.**
28	- `non_triviality` — does it add a fact/reading absent from подстрочник + tier-1 + Phase-1? Restates
29	  the crib ⇒ 0. **Gate: ≥1, else `park`.**
30	- `contrastive_value` — ≥2 commentators genuinely contrasted OR a translation choice resolved ⇒ 2;
31	  single commentator with real exegetical gain ⇒ 1; ornament ⇒ 0. **0 ⇒ `park` unless
32	  non_triviality = 2.**
33	- `register` — ЛП contract (§3.1): 1–3 sentences, terse, commentator named, IAST lemma, no
34	  Devanagari, no essay. Fixable wording ⇒ 1 (verdict `edit` + say what to fix). **Gate: ≥1.**
35	- `anchoring` — from `pratika_check` of the bundle: verified (pratīka or content anchor) ⇒ 2;
36	  unverified but plausible ⇒ 1; contradicted (`suggest_verse` points elsewhere and the note's
37	  content fits that other verse) ⇒ 0 ⇒ verdict `flag_anchor`.
38	
39	Verdicts: `keep` · `edit` · `park` · `reject` · `flag_anchor` (precedence: reject over flag_anchor
40	over park over edit over keep). You NEVER delete a note and NEVER clear `review_required` — you
41	rank for the human gate.
42	
43	## Output
44	
45	Rewrite `data/analysis/phase2_batch3/sarga_NN_candidates.json` IN PLACE, adding to each note a
46	`judge` object:
47	
48	```json
49	"judge": {"scores": {"faithfulness": 2, "non_triviality": 2, "contrastive_value": 1,
50	                     "register": 2, "anchoring": 2},
51	          "verdict": "keep", "reason": "…",
52	          "judged_by": "claude-sonnet-5", "step": "phase2_batch3_judge", "date": "2026-07-07"}
53	```
54	
55	Do not modify any other field, do not reorder arrays, keep UTF-8 no BOM (`ensure_ascii=False,
56	indent=2`). Update `_meta` with `"judged": true` and verdict counts. Do NOT run git. Return one
57	line per sarga: `sarga NN judged: N notes → keep K / edit E / park P / reject R / flag_anchor F`.
58	
59	_Auto-generated for the H268 batch-3 run; judging Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`), orchestration
60	Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`)._
61

1	# Phase-2 method manual — Sundarakāṇḍa commentator-dialogue layer
2	
3	_Created: 01-07-2026 · Last updated: 07-07-2026_
4	
5	> **What this is:** the complete, reproducible procedure for generating the Type-Б/В
6	> "commentator-dialogue" note layer for the Russian Sundarakāṇḍa — every step, *when* it runs, *how* to
7	> run it, and *why* it is done that way. Written so M.G./Kostina can review and correct the method **before
8	> it is scaled** past the 2026-07-01 pilot (sargas 35/36/37).
9	>
10	> Companion docs: [`docs/PHASE2_SUNDARA_HANDOFF.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/PHASE2_SUNDARA_HANDOFF.md)
11	> (scope + decisions) · [`SUNDARA_COMMENTARY_RATIONALE.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/SUNDARA_COMMENTARY_RATIONALE.md)
12	> (Phase-1 ledger) · [`data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md) (rights).
13	
14	## 0. Why this layer exists
15	
16	Phase-1 reached ~24 % density (Grintser level) using **dictionary** glosses. Phase-2 adds what a dictionary
17	cannot: what the **traditional Sanskrit commentators** (Tilaka, Bhūṣaṇa, Śiromaṇi) actually *say* about a
18	verse — a disambiguation, a supplied ellipsis, a textual variant, a myth behind a simile, a doctrinal
19	frame. The goal is to put Leonov's translation into dialogue with the ṭīkā tradition, in the register of
20	the «Литературные памятники» series (Grintser's Rāmāyaṇa is the benchmark), moving toward Leonov's own
21	~36 % density. **Depth, not bulk** — see §6 on why the accept rate is deliberately low.
22	
23	## 1. Pipeline at a glance
24	
25	```
26	data/valmiki_commentaries/kanda_5_sundarakanda/{tilaka,bhusana,siromani}_sarga_NN.txt   (licensed source)
27	        │  STEP 1 — deterministic segmentation (Opus-written Python, no LLM)
28	        ▼
29	data/analysis/sundara_commentary_segmented.json   (per-verse: verse + подстрочник + 3 commentaries)
30	        │  STEP 2 — candidate drafting (Sonnet subagents, 1 per sarga, parallel, write-only)
31	        ▼
32	data/analysis/phase2_pilot/sarga_NN_candidates.json   ({notes[], rejected[]}, all review_required)
33	        │  STEP 3 — deterministic merge + reject taxonomy (Opus-written Python)
34	        ▼
35	data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_candidates.json  +  pilot_rejected.json  +  PILOT_REVIEW.md
36	        │  STEP 4 — HUMAN GATE (Leonov/Kostina): accept / edit / reject each note
37	        ▼
38	data/sundara_ch{NN}_commentary_to_add.json (accepted, stamped)  +  *.rejected.json (with reason)
39	```
40	
41	**Model division (reported per project convention — tier AND version):**
42	- Orchestration + all deterministic code + this manual: **Opus 4.8** (`claude-opus-4-8`).
43	- Sanskrit→Russian note drafting: **Sonnet 5** (`claude-sonnet-5`), one subagent per sarga.
44	- The human gate: M.G. + E. Kostina. Nothing reaches the book without it.
45	
46	## 2. STEP 1 — deterministic segmentation
47	
48	**When:** first, once per batch of sargas. **Why deterministic:** splitting commentary by verse is
49	mechanical and must be reproducible/auditable — no LLM judgment belongs here.
50	
51	**How:**
52	```sh
53	python scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py            # pilot sargas 35 36 37
54	python scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py 22 24 26   # any sargas
55	```
56	[`scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/extract_yellow_sargas.py)
57	splits each commentary file on its `।। 5.<sarga>.<verse> ।।` markers (text *before* a marker glosses that
58	verse), aligns each verse with the IAST verse text and Leonov's подстрочник from the sibling
59	`SamudraManthanam` corpus, and writes per-verse bundles.
60	
61	**Pilot output:** 253 verse-bundles (70 with all three commentaries, 204 corpus-aligned, 48 merged-range
62	markers).
63	
64	**Known caveats (carry into the gate):**
65	- **Merged-range markers**: the source sometimes emits one marker for a verse range, scraped as a single
66	  token (e.g. `5.35.810` = vv. 8–10). These are flagged `ambiguous_marker: true` and don't align to a
67	  single passage; almost all are rejected in Step 2.
68	- **Marker offset glitch**: at least one verse (5.36.45) had its Bhūṣaṇa chunk actually belonging to v. 4.
69	  Isolated, and it produced no accepted note — but it is why **verse_ids must be verified against print**.
70	
71	## 3. STEP 2 — candidate drafting (Sonnet subagents)
72	
73	**When:** after Step 1, once the segmented JSON exists. **Why an LLM:** distilling Devanagari commentary
74	prose into a terse Russian ЛП note is a translation/judgment task, not a lookup. **Why Sonnet:** strong at
75	Sanskrit→Russian; and driven *inside Claude Code* it needs no API key (this sidesteps the repo's
76	"no-Anthropic-key" constraint, which governs only the standalone `scripts/annotate_batch.py` pipeline —
77	see §8). **Why one small agent per sarga, write-only:** the host process cycles and kills long agents;
78	small parallel agents each writing one file avoid git-index races and are resumable. This mirrors the
79	Phase-1 lesson.
80	
81	**How:** the orchestrator (Opus) spawns N Sonnet subagents, each given the style contract below, the
82	resolved decisions, the input path, and an output schema; each writes exactly
83	`data/analysis/phase2_pilot/sarga_NN_candidates.json` and returns a count summary. No agent runs git.
84	
85	### 3.1 Style contract (the ЛП register — non-negotiable)
86	
87	> **Contrastive-first (H268 decision 3, M.G. 07-07-2026).** The volume's distinguishing feature is
88	> Leonov's commentator-dialogue layer, so the agent's **preferred output form is the contrastive
89	> note** — «в „Тилаке“ — X; в „Широмани“ — Y; перевод следует …» — emitted **wherever the ṭīkā
90	> corpus shows ≥2 commentators diverging on the same verse**, with the reading the translation
91	> actually took named explicitly («переводчик следует Тилаке»; «волевое решение переводчика», where
92	> the translation goes against the ṭīkās — compare `leonov_ru` against the divergent readings).
93	> A single-commentator gloss is the **fallback**, not the default: draft it only when one
94	> commentator alone resolves a real translation choice, textual variant, ellipsis, or myth.
95	> Cite in Leonov's own hierarchy: **Тилака** first (≈70 % of his citations), **Бхушана** as
96	> counterpoint, **Широмани** for figurative readings, **Таттвадипика** for hard compounds
97	> (available for sargas 1–6), «Амритакатака» only for especially disputed passages (not in corpus —
98	> never invent it).
99	
100	- 1–3 sentences, затекстовое примечание. Terse. No essay, no Devanagari, no block quotes.
101	- Russian scholarly voice — *distil* the commentator, do not translate his Sanskrit syntax.
102	- **Name the commentator in-note** («по Тилаке», «Бхушана поясняет…») — decision [D-P2-2]; this is tier-2
103	  of model II. (Hard-rule #4 forbids naming them in the *article title* only — not in the apparatus.)
104	- Short **IAST pratīka** lemma; keep IAST ≈12 % of the note (Grintser calibration) — decision [D-P2-3].
105	  Under the ЛП calibration (H268 decision 2) the *merged* apparatus trends toward Leonov's own
106	  register (mean ≈310 chars); the per-note ≈12 % IAST share stays, but do not artificially shorten
107	  a contrastive note that needs its second clause.
108	- Kazansky type per note: **Б** = textological (wording / meaning / ellipsis / variant); **В** =
109	  realia/historical-cultural (place, custom, myth, epithet). Realia → В, never Б.
110	- **`why_proposed`** (required label): one clause stating *why this note earns a place* — what it gives
111	  beyond the подстрочник (the acceptance rationale, mirror image of a reject reason). The reviewer sees
112	  this label first. Pilot notes were back-filled by Opus (`scripts/backfill_why_proposed.py`); future
113	  agents emit it natively.
114	- Obey `validate.py` hard rules: never «М.: Наука 2022» for Leonov; «Парибка» is the only oblique form.
115	
116	### 3.2 What to draft vs. skip — the reject discipline
117	Draft a note **only** when the commentary adds something **neither the подстрочник NOR Leonov/Kostina's
118	own note** already gives. **Reject** when it (a) restates the подстрочник, (b) duplicates a Leonov/Kostina
119	own note on the same verse+point (see §3.3), (c) is pure Sanskrit grammar/parsing invisible to a Russian
120	reader, (d) is formulaic praise, (e) is a non-independent merged-range marker, or (f) duplicates an
121	earlier note. Every rejection is **kept with its reason** (§6).
122	
123	### 3.3 Dedup baseline — Leonov/Kostina's OWN apparatus (model II tier-1)
124	Leonov/Kostina already wrote **1,058 notes** across all 68 sargas (their print apparatus — this *is* the
125	~36 % density benchmark, and model II tier-1). Digitized by
126	[`scripts/extract_leonov_notes.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/extract_leonov_notes.py)
127	from `ramayana-leonov/Рамаяна. Книга 5. Сундараканда 2026.html` →
128	[`data/leonov_own_notes.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/leonov_own_notes.json)
129	(442 attributed to Kostina, 616 unattributed = Leonov; ~1,022 verses covered).
130	**Every Phase-2 candidate must be checked against this file** — a commentator note that repeats a point
131	Leonov/Kostina already made is a duplicate. **The 2026-07-01 pilot did NOT have this baseline** (agents
132	deduped only against the подстрочник): 9 of the 16 candidates landed on verses Leonov already comments on,
133	and several (e.g. 5.37.25 nāgarājasya, 5.35.82 Śambasādana, 5.36.17 upāya, 5.36.33 Śachī) are effective
134	duplicates. The interactive review page now shows Leonov's own note per verse in red so the reviewer sees
135	the overlap; when scaling, the drafting prompt must include the sarga's Leonov notes as dedup context.
136	
137	### 3.4 STEP 2b — LLM-as-judge scoring (H268 WS-C1; ACL-informed, added 07-07-2026)
138	
139	**When:** after drafting, before the review sheet is built. **Why:** the reject taxonomy showed
140	~67 % of drafter rejects are "restates the crib" — the same failure mode slips *into* accepted
141	candidates at some rate, and a heuristic filter can't measure faithfulness. The judge converts the
142	adversarial filter into a scored rubric so the printed note set is *earned* (see
143	[`docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/docs/ACL_METHODS_ADOPTED.md)
144	for the literature each design choice comes from).
145	
146	Design (each choice bias-motivated):
147	- **Pointwise, rubric-anchored, reason-then-score** (G-Eval pattern) — no pairwise comparisons, so
148	  no position bias; anchors below, not a bare 1–10 scale.
149	- **Refute-framed**: the judge's default is *park*; a note must earn `keep`. Counters judge
150	  leniency/verbosity bias and matches the layer's adversarial-filter tradition.
151	- **Drafter ≠ judge**: a fresh agent instance judges, never the drafting instance
152	  (self-preference mitigation).
153	- **The judge ranks; the human gates.** Verdicts partition candidates for the review sheet —
154	  nothing loses `review_required` and nothing is deleted; `park` verdicts stay visible with scores.
155	
156	Rubric (0–2 each; **gates, not a sum** — one axis can veto):
157	
158	| Axis | 2 | 1 | 0 | Gate |
159	|---|---|---|---|---|
160	| `faithfulness` | every claim entailed by the cited commentary text | minor overreach in wording | misstates / invents | **must be 2** — else `reject` |
161	| `non_triviality` | adds a fact/reading absent from подстрочник + tier-1 + Phase-1 | partially new | restates the crib | ≥1 — else `park` |
162	| `contrastive_value` | ≥2 commentators contrasted OR translation-choice resolved | single commentator, real exegetical gain | ornament | 0 ⇒ `park` unless non_triviality = 2 |
163	| `register` | ЛП contract (§3.1) holds | fixable wording (→ `edit`) | essay/anachronism | ≥1 — else `edit` |
164	| `anchoring` | segmenter verified (pratīka ∪ content anchor) | unverified, plausible | contradicted (`suggest_verse` elsewhere) | 0 ⇒ `flag_anchor` |
165	
166	Verdicts: `keep` (all gates pass) · `edit` (register-only issues) · `park` (fails
167	non-triviality/contrastive gates) · `reject` (faithfulness < 2) · `flag_anchor` (anchoring
168	contradicted — never print without a human fixing the verse). Judge output per note:
169	`judge: {scores, verdict, reason}` merged into the candidates JSON; the review page shows it.
170	
171	## 4. STEP 3 — merge + reject taxonomy
172	
173	**When:** after all sargas in the batch are drafted. **How:**
174	```sh
175	python scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py
176	```
177	[`scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/merge_phase2_pilot.py)
178	combines the per-sarga files into
179	[`pilot_candidates.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_candidates.json)
180	(all notes) and
181	[`pilot_rejected.json`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/pilot_rejected.json)
182	(all rejections, each tagged with a reason **bucket**), and asserts every note is `review_required`.
183	
184	## 5. STEP 4 — the human gate (this is where you come in)
185	
186	**When:** now, before any scale-up. **Interactive — no printing.** Build and open the review page:
187	```sh
188	python scripts/build_pilot_review_html.py     # -> data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html
189	```
190	Open [`data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_pilot/review.html)
191	in a browser. Each card shows: the verse (IAST + Leonov подстрочник), the **`why_proposed`** label,
192	the proposed note, the **Sanskrit source** (all three commentators at that verse; the cited one
193	highlighted), **neighbouring verses ±2** (so you see what else is commented nearby), and any existing
194	Phase-1 note on the verse. Click **✅ принять / ✏️ править / ❌ отклонить** per card (edit box and
195	reject-reason field appear as needed). Choices persist in `localStorage`; **⬇ Скачать decisions.json**
196	exports them (or ⧉ copy). The static markdown sheet `PILOT_REVIEW.md` remains as a read-only fallback.
197	
198	**Caveat shown in the page:** the per-verse "source" is the segmenter's alignment; because of marker
199	offsets/merged ranges it can differ from where the drafter actually found the cited text (e.g. 5.35.45
200	cites Tilaka but Tilaka's chunk aligned to a neighbour) — the neighbours panel is there to cover this.
201	
202	**After you send `decisions.json` back:** an apply step (to be written) grafts `accept`/`edit` notes into
203	`data/sundara_ch{NN}_commentary_to_add.json` with a `gated_by`/`gated_date` stamp and the (possibly edited)
204	text; `reject` entries go to a `.rejected.json` with your reason. Only once you approve the **register** do
205	we scale.
206	
207	## 6. Why the accept rate is ~6 % (and why that is correct)
208	
209	Pilot: **16 accepted of 253 considered (6.3 %); 138 rejections.** Reject taxonomy:
210	
211	| bucket | count | meaning |
212	|---|---:|---|
213	| restates_podstrochnik | 92 | commentary just re-says what Leonov already conveys |
214	| merged_range_marker | 25 | non-independent verse-range token, no single-verse gloss |
215	| pure_grammar | 12 | Sanskrit parsing invisible/irrelevant to a Russian reader |
216	| overlaps_other_note | 4 | point already made in a drafted note for a nearby verse |
217	| other | 3 | paraphrase-only / variant-without-gloss / speech-marker |
218	| formulaic_panegyric | 1 | ornamental praise, no exegesis |
219	| data_misalignment | 1 | the 5.36.45 marker-offset glitch |
220	
221	The headline finding: **two-thirds of all commentary simply restates the подстрочник.** That is expected —
222	a commentator-dialogue layer is inherently sparse, because most verses are not textually contested. This
223	layer is for **depth on the hard verses**, not density. The bulk of the ~36 % target will come from the
224	already-built lexical layer, not from this one. A *high* accept rate here would be the warning sign (it
225	would mean padding), exactly as the Phase-1 lexical gate proved.
226	
227	## 7. Count reconciliation (honesty note)
228	
229	`notes (16) + reject-entries (138) = 154 ≠ 253 verses considered`. The gap is because the drafters grouped
230	some rejects (e.g. one entry `5.35.17-20` covers four verses) and some considered bundles were
231	merged-range markers counted once. This is bookkeeping fuzz, **not** dropped data. When scaling, prefer
232	per-verse reject entries so the arithmetic closes.
233	
234	## 8. Provenance, rights & reproducibility
235	
236	- **Provenance:** every note carries `provenance: {model: "claude-sonnet-5", tier: "Sonnet", step:
237	  "phase2_pilot_draft"}` and `review_required: true`. The reject log records the drafter's reason.
238	- **Decision logs (added 04-07-2026, MG request):** each drafting batch preserves the agents' FULL
239	  transcripts — the verse-by-verse draft/reject reasoning — in the repo via
240	  [`scripts/export_agent_logs.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/export_agent_logs.py)
241	  → `data/analysis/<batch>/logs/` (raw `.jsonl` + readable `*_reasoning.md` per sarga +
242	  orchestrator extract; see the batch-2
243	  [logs/README.md](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_batch2/logs/README.md)).
244	  Run it at batch close-out **while the session cache is still alive** — the source transcripts
245	  live in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/` and are otherwise lost. The raw main
246	  session transcript is never committed (it embeds injected private context); only the
247	  orchestrator's own messages are extracted.
248	- **Reproducibility caveat:** because the pilot was drafted by Sonnet *inside Claude Code*, the committed
249	  standalone `scripts/` cannot reproduce the exact note texts without Claude Code. Steps 1, 3 (Python) are
250	  fully deterministic and reproducible; Step 2 (drafting) is model-mediated and human-gated, so the record
251	  is the committed candidate files + this manual, not a re-runnable keyless script. Anyone without Claude
252	  Code can reproduce the drafting via the repo's openai-compat backend (`scripts/annotate_batch.py`,
253	  DeepSeek etc.) — the "no Anthropic key" rule applies to that path.
254	- **Rights:** commentary source is the Gita Supersite corpus, used by permission (CC BY 4.0). Any
255	  redistribution carries the attribution string from [`data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/valmiki_PERMISSION.md).
256	
257	## 9. Scaling plan (only after the pilot register is approved)
258	
259	1. Run Step 1 on the next batch — the 14 🟡 sargas first (22, 24, 26, 30, 34, 35–37, 39, 51), then 🔴/⚪.
260	2. Fold any register corrections from the gate into the Step-2 style contract before drafting more.
261	3. Draft (Sonnet, ≤3–4 parallel agents), merge, gate — same loop.
262	4. Track cumulative density in `data/sundara_book_stats.json`; stop the *commentator* layer when its
263	   marginal accept rate collapses (dry signal), not at a fixed count.
264	5. Switch to per-verse reject entries (§7) so counts reconcile at scale.
265	
266	## 11. Alignment accuracy — current state & preprocessing plan
267	
268	**Current (marker-only) accuracy.** Step 1 aligns commentary to verses solely by the `।। 5.s.v ।।`
269	markers. Pilot: **204/253 (~81 %) of bundles corpus-aligned**; 48 merged-range markers. Per-commentator
270	alignment is weaker — e.g. 5.35.45 cites Tilaka, but Tilaka's chunk aligned to a neighbour/merged token.
271	Two failure modes: (a) **merged-range tokens** (`5.35.810` = vv. 8–10) don't map to one verse; (b)
272	**marker offsets** (a chunk sits before the wrong marker, e.g. 5.36.45 held v. 4's text).
273	
274	**Yes — accuracy can be materially improved, mostly by preprocessing** (documented now, to implement before
275	scaling):
276	1. **Merged-range reconstruction.** Parse tokens like `810` using sequence context (prev marker 7, next 11
277	   ⇒ 8–10); attribute the chunk to each verse in the range and tag `verse_range`. Repairs most of the 48.
278	2. **Sequence validation + offset repair.** Cross-check the marker sequence against the canonical verse
279	   count per sarga (e.g. 90 for sarga 35); flag out-of-order/duplicate markers and snap them to the
280	   expected position. Catches the 5.36.45-type offset.
281	3. **Pratīka anchoring (strongest signal).** Every traditional gloss opens with a *pratīka* — the verse
282	   catchword it comments (e.g. `yānīti` = yāni + iti). Match the pratīka against the verse's own words
283	   (transliteration-normalized, via the org `sanskrit-util` toolkit — do not re-implement transcoding) to
284	   align **by content**, independent of the `।।` marker. This would have placed Tilaka on 5.35.45
285	   correctly. Define **alignment precision = fraction of chunks whose pratīka matches the assigned verse**;
286	   target > 95 %.
287	4. **Keep multi-glosses.** A verse can carry several sub-glosses (bhūṣaṇa emitted 131 markers for 90
288	   verses) — preserve all, don't collapse.
289	
290	Until this lands, the mitigation is the review page's **neighbours ±2** panel and the honest per-page
291	caveat. Recommended order: implement (1)+(2) as a cheap `extract_yellow_sargas.py` preprocessing pass,
292	then (3) as a validation/repair step reported alongside the segmented output.
293	
294	**IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-01 (partial):** shared canon module `scripts/sa_align.py` (wraps `sanskrit_util`
295	`nfold` + `difflib`; SHARED_CODE §1-2). Wired into `compare_editions.py` (principled canon; identical
296	1006→1065; transposition detection; true-vs-apparent absence split — but `critical_only` stayed ~399,
297	needs fuzzy global assignment, not done) and into `extract_yellow_sargas.py` as pratīka anchoring: each
298	gloss's leading pratīka is deva→iast→canon'd and prefix-matched to the verse; the run now reports
299	`alignment_precision`. **Measured: 0.432** (197/456) with prefix matching — well below the >95% target,
300	and 138/259 mismatches carry a `suggest_verse` (a nearby verse the pratīka fits) → the marker-based
301	segmentation has a systematic offset recoverable by a **reassignment pass (item 3, NOT yet done)**. So
302	p.1 delivered the shared canon + honest metrics + edition correctness, but neither aspirational target
303	(critical_only <50, precision >95%) is met yet.
304	
305	**Item 1a (fuzzy assigner) 2026-07-01 — done, corrected conclusion.** Token-set Jaccard pass pairing
306	mutually-unmatched verses recovered only 22 clean pairs (critical_only 399→377). A sample diagnostic
307	showed the residual is NOT artifact: those critical verses map to nearby southern verses at Jaccard
308	0.27–0.44 — the **same shlokas heavily reworded** between Baroda critical and southern vulgate. The "<50"
309	premise was wrong (the recensions rephrase pervasively). The useful output instead **partitions the 742
310	southern-only into `structural_absence` (307, best Jaccard vs any critical verse < 0.25 → real absence,
311	safe footnote) vs `reworded` (435, 0.25–0.5 → variant reading, NOT an absence)** — the real accuracy win
312	for footnotes (item 4): only the 307 + whole extra sargas are truly "absent in critical."
313	
314	**Item 3 completion — content anchor (H268 WS-C2, 07-07-2026).** The residual ~10 % (pronominal
315	pratīkas + paraphrasing ṭīkās) is now covered by a second, independent signal: **containment** —
316	the fraction of the verse's canon tokens echoed anywhere in the chunk (`sa_align.containment`;
317	asymmetric on purpose, so chunk length doesn't dilute the score, unlike Jaccard). Where the leading
318	pratīka matches no verse, the chunk is (a) *moved* to a ±3-window verse only on a clear margin
319	(containment ≥ 0.20 and ≥ 0.08 over the current verse), and (b) *verified* in place when the
320	current verse is the local containment argmax at ≥ 0.15. Two precisions are now reported honestly:
321	`alignment_precision` (strict pratīka-only, old definition — **0.888** on the 10 gated sargas,
322	unchanged) and `alignment_precision_verified` (pratīka ∪ content — **0.964** on the 10 gated
323	sargas, **0.945** across the 58 batch-3 sargas), clearing the H268 >0.90 print-safety target.
324	Chunks failing both signals keep `suggest_verse` and are surfaced to the judge (§3.4 `flag_anchor`)
325	and the review page; nothing unverified prints without a human. Tattvadīpikā (sargas 1–6) was also
326	added as a fourth segmented commentator.
327	
328	**Item 1b (segmenter reassignment) 2026-07-01 — done.** `extract_yellow_sargas.py` now re-anchors each
329	commentary chunk to the verse its leading pratīka actually matches (nearest in the sarga), fixing the
330	systematic marker offset instead of only flagging it. **179 chunks reassigned; pratīka alignment precision
331	0.432 → 0.799 → 0.896** (353/394) after adding **iti-stemming** to the matcher (a pratīka is quoted fused
332	with *iti*: `rakṣitā+iti`→`raksiteti`; stripping `-iti/-eti/-ti` yields a stem that prefix-matches the
333	verse word). The residual ~10% (41 chunks) is the genuinely-hard set and is left as-is (diminishing
334	returns): 11 bare-pronoun pratīkas ("sa"/"te") and ~30 Tilaka/Śiromaṇi *paraphrases* that don't quote a
335	verse word. Reassignment is heuristic; all downstream notes stay `review_required`.
336	
337	## 10. Decision & change record
338	
339	- 2026-07-01 — C0/D2 = model II (two-tier hybrid); D-P2-1 pilot 35/36/37; D-P2-2 name commentator in-note;
340	  D-P2-3 RU + IAST pratīka; D-P2-4 hybrid (Sonnet drafts, human gates); D-P2-5 ~36 % post-approval.
341	- 2026-07-01 — pilot drafted (16 notes), reject log consolidated + taxonomy added; awaiting human gate.
342	- 2026-07-03 — **pilot gated by M.G.: 16/16 passed** (9 accept / 7 edit / 0 reject). Edit-directives
343	  («объединить с комментарием Костиной») preserved as `gate.mg_comment`, note text kept clean.
344	- 2026-07-04 — decisions applied by [`scripts/apply_phase2_decisions.py`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/scripts/apply_phase2_decisions.py)
345	  (the §5 apply step, now written): grafted into ch35/36/37 + book aggregate with `gate` stamps,
346	  `review_required` stays true until the Leonov/Kostina assembly gate. **Scale batch 2 drafted**
347	  (H142): sargas 22/24/26/30/34/39/51, 38 candidates / 350 verses (10.9%), per-verse rejects (§7
348	  fixed — counts reconcile exactly), tier-1 dedup context in every drafting prompt (§3.3 satisfied;
349	  41 rejects bucketed `duplicate_of_tier1`), pratīka precision 0.889 across all 10 yellow sargas.
350	  Review page: [`data/analysis/phase2_batch2/review.html`](https://github.com/gasyoun/CommentaryStrategies/blob/main/data/analysis/phase2_batch2/review.html).
351	  Drafting Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`), orchestration Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`).
352	- 2026-07-07 — **H268 (ЛП camera-ready reset): §3.1 rewritten contrastive-first** (decision 3 —
353	  preferred output = «в „Тилаке“ X / в „Широмани“ Y / перевод следует …», single-commentator gloss
354	  demoted to fallback; Leonov citation hierarchy made explicit; Tattvadīpikā added for sargas 1–6);
355	  **§3.4 LLM-as-judge rubric added** (WS-C1 — pointwise refute-framed scoring, drafter ≠ judge,
356	  faithfulness veto); **§11 item 3 closed by the content anchor** (WS-C2 — verified precision
357	  0.964/0.945, strict pratīka metric kept unchanged at 0.888). Batch-3 = the remaining 58 sargas,
358	  drafted per-sarga off `data/analysis/phase2_batch3/segmented/`. Orchestration Fable 5
359	  (`claude-fable-5`), drafting/judging Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`).
360	
361	_Dr. Mārcis Gasūns_
362

**Judging sarga 19 notes:**

1. **5.19.5** (`saṃśitavratām`): Tilaka reads it as a specific vow for Ravana's death, vs Phase-1 note which gives the Kashyapa formulaic-epithet parallel (ascetic overtone via MBh). Note gives concrete content of the vow (Ravana's death) — different angle from Phase-1's formulaic epithet parallel. Checking bundle: Tilaka's text = "संशितव्रतां रावणवधाय तीक्ष्णं व्रतमिव कुर्वाणाम्" — "saṃśitavratāṃ [as if] performing an intense vrata for the killing of Rāvaṇa" — matches note's claim exactly. Faithful (2). Non-trivial vs Phase-1 (2, different angle). Contrastive: single commentator (1). Register: clean, 1 sentence, names Tilaka, IAST lemma present, no Devanagari (2). Anchoring: pratika_check shows tilaka matches_verse true (2). Verdict: keep.

2. **5.19.6** (`maṇḍanārhām amaṇḍanām`): Note claims Tilaka resolves the paradox (dirt = ornament of ascetic) AND cites a variant reading "citrāṅgī" by "Tīrtha". Bundle text: "मलेन मण्डनस्थानेषु दिग्धाङ्गीं रूषिताङ्गीम् । "चित्राङ्गीम्" इति पठित्वा मलरूपेण मण्डनेन चित्राङ्गीं कर्बुरामित्यर्थं तीर्थ आह । संन्यासित्वादुचितैव तस्य मले ऽपि मण्डनत्वबुद्धिः" — This matches well: Tīrtha reads "citrāṅgīm" and Tilaka's own comment about संन्यासित्व justifying dirt-as-ornament. Faithful (2). Non-trivial (2 — new variant + doctrinal resolution not in подстрочник/Phase-1). **5.20.6**: Note claims Tilaka's variant reading "evaṃ caitad akāmāṃ tvām" shifts the meaning to Ravana's restraint being a rakshasa-dharma rule rather than personal choice. Bundle Tilaka text confirms: "\"एवं चैतदकामां त्वाम्\" इति पाठे एतद्रक्षोधर्मत्वम्" = "In the reading 'evaṃ caitad akāmāṃ tvām', this [is stated to be] the rakshasa-dharma-ness [of it]." Register clean (2). Anchoring: tilaka pratika_check `matches_verse: true` → 2. **Verdict: keep**.

Now let me judge the 3 notes.

**5.29.1** (`tathāgatāṃ tāṃ vyathitām`): Note claims Bhushana reads "tathā" not as neutral but as marking extremity of grief, citing Sita's own earlier words about 12 peaceful years. Bundle Bhushana: "तां धर्मिस्वरूपातिरिक्तयत्किंचिदतिशयरहिताम् । व्यथिताम् ... तथा च पूर्वोक्तं सर्वं धर्मिस्वरूपमात्रम् । इतः परमेव व्यसनानि भविष्यन्तीति मन्यमानाम् । "समा द्वादश तत्राहं राघवस्य निवेशने । भुञ्जाना मानुषान् भोगान् सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी ।" इत्युक्तं भोगजातं सर्वमकिंचित्करमासीत्, दुःखमेव निरूपकमासीत्" — matches note precisely, including the verbatim 12-years quote ("samā dvādaśa tatrāhaṃ rāghavasya niveśane bhuñjānā mānuṣān bhogān sarvakāmasamṛddhinī"). Faithful (2). Non-trivial vs подстрочник/tier-1 (tier-1 has no note on this verse)/Phase-1 (Phase-1's note on this verse is about "nimitta" term generally, not this specific narrative-callback point) — 2. Contrastive_value: single commentator, real narrative-callback gain = 1. Register clean (2). Anchoring: bhusana pratika `matches_verse: true` → 2. **Verdict: keep**.

**5.29.5** (`śikharāgradantyāḥ`): Note claims Bhushana adds a samudrika-śāstra (body-signs science) doctrine that teeth-like-pomegranate-seeds ensure the husband's longevity. Bundle Bhushana: "शिखरदन्तत्वे सामुद्रिकम् "स्निग्धास्समानुरूपाः सुपङ्क्तयः शिखरिणः श्लक्ष्णाः । दन्ता भवन्ति यासां तासां पादे जगत्सर्वम् ।।" इति, "यासां शिखरिणो दन्ता दीर्घं जीवन्ति ताः स्त्रियः" इति च" — this quotes samudrika verses about women with such teeth: "at whose feet the whole world [bows]" and "women whose teeth are śikhariṇa [pointed like pomegranate seeds] — their [husbands] live long" (यासां शिखरिणो दन्ता दीर्घं जीवन्ति ताः स्त्रियः — literally "those women whose teeth are śikhariṇa, [their husbands? they themselves?] live long" — the Sanskrit is ambiguous about whose longevity, but "तासां...दीर्घं जीवन्ति" more naturally parses with an implied husband subject in this genre of physiognomy verses about auspicious wife-signs). This is a defensible reading of the samudrika citation matching the note's claim. Faithful (2). Non-trivial vs Kostina's tier-1 note (which covers only the Tilaka translation of the compound + the "approaching lover" sign, not the samudrika longevity omen) and Phase-1 (no note on this verse) — 2. Contrastive_value: single commentator, real doctrinal addition = 1. Register clean (2). Anchoring: bhusana pratika `matches_verse: true` → 2. **Verdict: keep**.

**5.29.7** (`bhrukeśāntam`): Note claims Bhushana explains the omitted compound "bhrukeśānta" as not just "brows and hair" but disheveled locks at the temples framing the upper face. Bundle Bhushana: "स्वक्षिभ्रुशोभनाक्षिश्रूयुक्तम् । केशाः अन्ते यस्य तत् केशान्तम् । उपरिभागप्रकीर्णालकमित्यर्थः" = "svakṣibhru = endowed with beautiful eyes and brows; keśānta = 'that which has hair at its end' — meaning locks scattered in the upper region." Matches note's claim well ("растрёпанные у висков пряди" — disheveled locks at the temples/upper region). Faithful (2). Non-trivial vs Kostina's note (which just flags the omission without content) — 2. Contrastive_value: single commentator = 1. Register clean (2). Anchoring: bhusana pratika `matches_verse: true` → 2. **Verdict: keep**.

content.text: Now let's check the segmented bundle for verses 9, 19 in sarga 31.

Confirmed for 5.31.9: Bhushana's chunk "मृगयां परिधावता मृगयामुद्दिश्य परिधावता । अनेन लीलया खरादिवधः सूच्यते" = "'mṛgayāṃ paridhāvatā' [means] roaming about for the purpose of hunting; by this [word] it is indicated that the killing of Khara etc. was [done] playfully (līlayā)." content.text:
This confirms 5.32.4, 5.32.6, and 5.32.8. Let's check note claims closely:

**5.32.4**: Note claims Tilaka: fear of illusion (māyā) recurrence, Siromani: longing for Rama (rāmātismṛtyā vaicittyam). Bundle Tilaka: "पुनरपि मायैवेयमिति भयान्मुमोह" = "again fainted from fear [thinking] 'this is māyā again'." Bundle Siromani: "अत एव दुर्निरीक्ष्यमिदमिति मत्वापि पुनर्मुमोह रामातिस्मृत्या वैचित्यं प्राप" = "even having thought 'this is hard to look upon,' she again fainted — she attained distraction through excessive remembrance of Rāma (rāmātismṛtyā vaicittyam)." Matches note exactly, including verbatim quoted term. Faithful (2).

**5.32.6**: Note claims Tilaka+Siromani: Sita cries deliberately softly out of caution so rakshasis won't notice the unfamiliar monkey. Bundle Tilaka: "मन्दमन्दस्वरा । अस्य दैवगत्या वास्तवत्वे राक्षस्यो मा जानन्त्वित्यतिमन्दस्वररोदनम्" = "mandamandasvarā — [meaning] weeping in an extremely soft voice, [with the thought] 'may the rakshasis not know of this [monkey's] reality by chance'." Bundle Siromani: "मन्दस्वरेत्यनेनेमं वानरं राक्षस्यो न जानन्त्वित्यभिप्रायः सूचितः" = "by 'mandasvara' the intention 'may the rakshasis not know of this monkey' is indicated." Matches note exactly. Faithful (2).

**5.32.8**: Note claims Tilaka+Siromani: Sita faints because she thinks this is Ravana in disguise again. Bundle Tilaka: "सा तं कपिरूपं रावणमित्येव समीक्ष्य भृशं विसञ्ज्ञा" = "having beheld him thinking 'this monkey-form is indeed Rāvaṇa,' she became extremely unconscious." Bundle Siromani: "तं हनूमन्तं समीक्ष्य रावणत्वेन वितर्क्य गतासुकल्पा" = "having beheld Hanumān and inferred [him to be] Rāvaṇa, she became as if lifeless." Matches note exactly. Faithful (2).

This Bhushana chunk is filed under an `ambiguous_marker: true` bundle labeled `5.33.1213` (a merged-range token), and it gives: "व्यञ्जनामि स्तनजघनादीनि" = "vyañjanāni [means] the breasts, hips, etc." and "लक्षणानि शुभावर्तरेखादिसामुद्रिकलक्षणानि" = "lakṣaṇāni [means] auspicious spiral-lines etc., the technical samudrika marks." This matches the note's claim about Bhushana precisely.

And Tilaka's chunk (filed under a separate `ambiguous_marker: true` bundle `5.33.1315`) says: "यतो व्यञ्जनानि राममहिषीत्वप्रकाशकानि ते सामुद्रिकालक्षणानि च लक्षये" — here Tilaka actually treats vyañjanāni and lakṣaṇāni somewhat together as "signs revealing her queenship" and "samudrika marks", which doesn't exactly show him drawing the sharp distinction the note claims ("Тилака и Бхушана в дальнейшем разборе уточняют иначе: вьянджана — это телесные черты (грудь, бёдра), а лакшана — формальные приметы саамудрики"). The note attributes this dual distinction to *both* Tilaka and Bhushana, but only Bhushana's chunk actually draws the vyañjana=body-parts vs lakṣaṇa=samudrika-marks distinction cleanly; Tilaka's chunk doesn't clearly separate the two terms this way — it uses both terms somewhat loosely together ("vyañjanāni ... te sāmudrikālakṣaṇāni ca lakṣaye" — reads more like he's treating them as a compound reference to the queenly signs generally, not explicitly splitting vyañjana from lakṣaṇa the way Bhushana does).

This is a moderate faithfulness concern: the note claims **both** Tilaka and Bhushana draw the same distinction ("Тилака и Бхушана в дальнейшем разборе уточняют иначе"), but only Bhushana's text supports this cleanly. This is a case of overstating which commentators hold a view — a form of overreach, though the substantive content (the vyañjana/lakṣaṇa distinction itself) is genuinely present and correctly attributed to Bhushana. I'll score this as **minor wording overreach = 1** for faithfulness (not full misattribution, but the note incorrectly co-attributes Tilaka to a distinction his text doesn't clearly draw), which caps the verdict at `edit` rather than `keep` (register/faithfulness overreach is fixable by narrowing the attribution to Bhushana alone, or by more carefully hedging).

The issue is that the note also claims Tilaka shares this same distinction, which is a stretch/overstatement rather than an invention — Tilaka's text does mention both terms in the same breath but doesn't clearly split them the way Bhushana does. Confirmed for 5.38.36 — Siromani's chunk verbatim: "दशरथाय नमस्कत्वेत्यनेन पलायनसमये दशरथोपदेशादेव रामशरणमागत इति ध्वनितम्" = "By [the crow's] bowing to Daśaratha, it is suggested that at the time of fleeing [the crow] came to Rāma's refuge precisely because of Daśaratha's advice [given to it in heaven]." Matches note precisely. Faithful (2).

Confirmed for 5.38.37 — Tilaka's chunk: "कस्माद्राक्षसक्षयं न करोतीत्यस्योत्तरम्-- त्वच्छोकेति । त्वद्वियोगजशोकेन सर्वकार्यविमुख इत्यर्थः" = "The answer to 'why does he not destroy the rakshasas': [the word] tvacchoka — [meaning] due to grief born of separation from you, he is averse to all [other] activity." Matches note precisely. This is Tilaka's answer to "why doesn't Rama destroy Ravana" and confirms both claims (not weakness, but grief-induced aversion to action). Faithful (2). Now let's check 65 and 68.

Excellent — I found the exact chunk. It's under 5.38.68 bundle, Tilaka's text: "गिरिवरपवनावधूतमुक्तः ... प्रभावात्सामर्थ्यविशेषात् । राक्षसीभिर्यथा न ज्ञायते तथा धृतम्" = "prabhāvāt = through [its] special power; it was held/kept such that the rakshasis would not notice [it]" — this confirms the note's claim exactly. This is filed under 5.38.68's Tilaka chunk (note's `verse_id` matches this correctly), and the drafter's own rejected-entry cross-reference for 5.38.66/5.38.70 explicitly acknowledges the split of Tilaka's material across verses (which is transparent, similar to sarga 27's pattern). Faithful (2).

Also for 5.38.65 — confirmed: Siromani reads Kauśikī as "kauśika-gotra-pṛthvī" (earth of Kauśika lineage, rescued by Varāha), and Bhushana reads it as Indra's royal Śrī (fortune), abducted to Pātāla after Vṛtra's slaying and restored by Nārāyaṇa, with an alternate Mahābhārata-based story about Utathya's wife also cited. This matches the note's claims about both commentators precisely, and the note correctly notes neither matches the lexical note's Kuśika-daughter/Viśvāmitra identification.

Confirmed for 5.40.23: Tilaka's chunk: "समाधानं संविधानम्, "अथापि स महाबाहुः" इति पाठे यथेत्यपि पूरणीयमेव । यद्यपि श्रुतवृत्तान्तः स्वयमेव यतिष्यति तथापि त्वमपि यथा मां शीघ्रं तारयसि तथा संविधानं कुर्वित्यर्थः" = "'samādhāna' [means] 'arrangement' (saṃvidhāna); [there is] a variant reading 'athāpi sa mahābāhuḥ' [instead of 'yathā ca sa mahābāhuḥ']... although, having heard the news, he [Rāma] will himself strive, still you too should make the arrangement so that you quickly rescue me." Then continues: "तत्कार्यं लङ्कागमनप्रयोजनमल्पशेषम् । देवीदर्शनरूपस्य महतः प्रधानकृत्यस्य निष्पन्नत्वात्परबलदर्शनरूपस्यानुषङ्गिकत्वादल्पशेषत्वम्" = "that task, the purpose of coming to Laṅkā, has little remaining — since the great main task (seeing the queen) is accomplished, the [remaining task of] observing enemy strength is secondary, hence little remains." content.text: Confirmed for 5.43.1: Tilaka's own chunk in this very bundle already says "चैत्यप्रासादो रक्षःकुलदेवताप्रासादः" (= "caitya-prāsāda is the temple-palace of the rakshasas' family deity") and Siromani's: "चैत्यप्रासादः राक्षसकुलदेवताधिष्ठानीभूतप्रासादविशेषः" (= "a special palace serving as the abode of the rakshasas' family deity"). But the note attributes this to Bhushana specifically ("по Бхушане... caityaṃ devāyatanam, tadrūpaḥ prāsādaḥ"). Let me check where the "5.43.34" bundle's Bhushana text actually gives this — since I need to see if Bhushana himself (not Tilaka/Siromani) makes this specific claim with that exact phrasing.

Found it precisely — the bundle labeled `5.43.34` (verse-token "34", `ambiguous_marker: false`) contains Bhushana's exact text: "चैत्यं देवायतनम्, तद्रूपः प्रासादः चैत्यप्रसादः तम्" = "caitya = devāyatana (abode of a deity); a palace in that form is a caitya-prāsāda." This matches the note's claim exactly, including the specific phrasing "caityaṃ devāyatanam, tadrūpaḥ prāsādaḥ" quoted almost verbatim. AND this same bundle continues: "प्रतिसूर्यः द्वितीयसूर्य इत्यर्थः । अनेन सूर्योदयस्सूचितः" = "pratisūrya means 'a second sun'; by this, sunrise is indicated (sūryodayaḥ sūcitaḥ)" — which matches note #2 (5.43.4) exactly as well. Both notes' content is fully confirmed here — faithful (2) for both.

Now let's check baselines.

content.text: Only one note. Let's check the segmented bundle for verse 2.

Confirmed precisely: Tilaka's chunk "परस्परजयैषिणो ऽहमहमिकया स्वस्वोत्कर्षापेक्षिणः" = "parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ — desiring their own individual superiority through mutual rivalry (ahamahamikā, 'I-first-ness')." Bhushana's chunk: "परस्परजयैषिणः प्रत्येकं हनुमज्जयैषिण इत्यर्थः" = "parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ — [meaning] each one individually desiring to defeat Hanumān." This matches the note precisely — Tilaka reads it as sibling rivalry among themselves, Bhushana reads it as each independently wanting to beat Hanuman. Faithful (2). The note also claims "перевод следует Тилаке" (the translation follows Tilaka) — checking Leonov's own Russian: "желающие превзойти друг друга" = "wanting to surpass each other" — this indeed matches Tilaka's mutual-rivalry reading, not Bhushana's each-vs-Hanuman reading. Confirmed.

Let's check baselines.
